title: Biomechanical mechanisms of chronic low back pain
summary:
Chronic low back pain is one of the most common causes of physical limitations and reduced quality of life worldwide. However, the underlying causes and mechanisms of chronic low back pain are still not fully understood. In particular, alterations in muscle activity, movement control, and spinal loading may play an important role.

The aim of this study is to improve the understanding of how movement patterns, muscle activity, and spinal control change in individuals with chronic low back pain and how these factors can be influenced by targeted training.

For this purpose, patients with chronic low back pain as well as healthy control participants will take part in a standardized training program. Participants will be assessed repeatedly:
before the training program,
during the training period,
after completion of the training,
and during follow-up assessments.

The examinations include motion analysis, measurements of muscle activity, gait analysis, imaging procedures, questionnaires regarding health and quality of life, and assessments of pain sensitivity.

The results of the study are intended to improve the understanding of the mechanisms underlying chronic low back pain and to support the development of improved diagnostic and therapeutic approaches in the future.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Ability to provide written informed consent
Ability to perform the functional, biomechanical, and training procedures required in the study
Sufficient German or English language skills to complete questionnaires and follow study instructions
For patient groups: chronic low back pain persisting for at least 3 months
For the asymptomatic control group: no current or chronic low back pain
Willingness to participate in all scheduled assessment time points, including follow-up examinations
Eligibility for MRI examinations
Willingness to participate in the standardized neuromuscular training program with EMG-based biofeedback over six weeks
Willingness to allow pseudonymized storage and scientific analysis of collected study data
Exclusion criteria:
Acute low back pain (< 3 months)
Specific spinal pathologies (e.g., tumor, fracture, infection, inflammatory spinal disease)
Previous spinal surgery within the last 12 months
Severe neurological disorders affecting movement or balance
Severe musculoskeletal disorders limiting participation in the training program or functional assessments
Severe cardiovascular, pulmonary, or systemic diseases contraindicating physical activity
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Contraindications for MRI examinations (e.g., pacemaker, ferromagnetic implants, severe claustrophobia)
Current participation in another interventional clinical study
Inability to comply with study procedures or follow study instructions
Insufficient German or English language skills to complete questionnaires and assessments
Current substance abuse or severe psychiatric disorders interfering with study participation
Any condition judged by the investigators to compromise safe participation or data quality
